footnotes.text: 4. The Carolina Core provides the common core of knowledge, skill and academic experience for all Carolina undergraduate students.

footnotes.text: 5. Statement of Purpose: If the Dean approves the student to apply to the BarSc. program, then the student prepares a “Statement of Purpose” and submits it to the Dean and an Associate Dean for review. That Statement of Purpose should contain the following information: • The student’s academic strengths and weaknesses; • The student’s personal and professional goals, both long- and short-term; • The reasons why the student’s academic and professional goals cannot be met through a standard degree program (for example, a double major).

No courses of a remedial, developmental, skill-acquiring, or vocational nature may apply as credit toward BarSc degree.

footnotes.text: 9. BarSC Appropriate Elective (4-45 hours): Students must take at least 69 honors credit hours, to include 45 honors core credit hours. To fulfill these requirements, courses must be listed as a “South Carolina Honors College” course. Requirements may be fulfilled by Carolina Core or BarSC major courses. For example, a student could take an Honors-designated major course or Carolina Core course and the course would fulfill the Honors requirement and major/Carolina Core requirement. Students may choose to fulfill these requirements in any way that works with their major or personal interests, meaning there is no specific order in which you must take certain classes. If courses taken to fulfil Carolina Core or BarSC major courses are not listed as a “South Carolina Honors College” Course, then Honors courses must be taken in addition to fulfill the requirements below: a. English or Literature (0-3 hours): One Honors course in English composition. b. History of Civilization (0-3 hours): Any Honors course on the history of civilization. c. Humanities (0-3 hours): Any Honors humanities course. d. Social Behavioral Science (0-3 hours): Any Honors social or behavioral science. e. Natural Science with lab (0-4 hours): Any Honors science course. Must include Honors lab. f. Analysis (0-3 hours): Math, logic, statistics, computer science, or other courses so designated. g. Honors Elective (0-19 hours): Any Honors courses or up to 6 credit hours of Study Abroad. h. Beyond the Classroom (0-3 hours): Undergraduate research, service learning, internship, or study away outside South Carolina (study away can be non-Honors). i. Thesis (4 hours): SCHC 390 – Proseminar (1 hour) and SCHC 499 – Senior Thesis/Project (3 hours)

footnotes.text: 11. BarSC Major Courses (3-24 hours): Students must take at least 69 honors credit hours, to include at least 24 major credit hours. The student’s BarSc. Committee meets with the student to design an individualized curriculum that has no major, minor, or cognate, but reflects the student’s interests, strengths, and weaknesses. Courses in addition to those displayed in the major map may be required, as decided by the BarSc. Committee. Major courses typically demonstrate depth and breadth of study in at least two academic disciplines.
